stories.headline: Assam Sahitya Sabha Election: Nayanmoni Choudhury Files Nomination for General Secretary Post
stories.title: Assam Sahitya Sabha Election: Nayanmoni Choudhury Files Nomination for General Secretary Post
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Guwahati: The preparations for the upcoming election to the post of General Secretary of the Assam Sahitya Sabha have gathered momentum, with candidate Nayanmoni Choudhury filing his nomination papers on 11th November.
Choudhury submitted his nomination at the Sabha’s central office, Bhagawati Prasad Barua Bhawan, in Guwahati.

He arrived at the office in a convoy of around 10 vehicles, accompanied by representatives of various branches of the Assam Sahitya Sabha and literary enthusiasts from different districts across the state.
A large number of supporters and Sabha representatives from different parts of Assam were present at the venue during the nomination process.
The gathering reflected the growing activity surrounding the upcoming election, with preparations gaining pace ahead of the selection of the organisation’s next General Secretary.
The Assam Sahitya Sabha, one of the state's prominent literary organisations, plays a significant role in promoting Assamese language, literature and culture.

stories.headline: Cabinet approves Rs 62,370 cr subsidy for P&K fertilisers in rabi season
stories.title: Cabinet approves Rs 62,370 cr subsidy for P&K fertilisers in rabi season
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 11: The government on Wednesday approved a Rs 62,370 crore subsidy on phosphatic and potassic (P&K) fertilisers for the rabi season 2026-27. The Union Cabinet, chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, approved the Department of Fertilizers' proposal to fix the Nutrient Based Subsidy (NBS) rates for Rabi season 2026-27 (from October 2026 to March 31, 2027) on Phosphatic and Potassic (P&K) fertilisers. The Cabinet has approved Rs 62,370 crore as subsidy for P&K fertilisers, Union Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw told reporters after the Cabinet meeting. He said the fertiliser prices have shot up immensely due to the West Asia crisis and the Russia-Ukraine war. However, the minister said the government has protected farmers' interests by providing adequate fertiliser subsidy. The Modi government has provided a shield to farmers from geopolitical turmoil, he added. Vaishnaw said the DAP (di-ammonium phosphate) rate would remain the same at Rs 1,350 per bag of 50 kg each. The subsidy on P&K fertilisers, including DAP and NPKS (Nitrogen, Phosphorus, Potash, Sulphur) grades, will be provided based on approved rates for Rabi 2026-27 to ensure smooth availability of these soil nutrients to the farmers at affordable prices.

stories.headline: Tamil Nadu may approach Supreme Court seeking greater powers for Cauvery Water Management Authority
stories.title: Tamil Nadu may approach Supreme Court seeking greater powers for Cauvery Water Management Authority
stories.summary: The State wants the Authority to be modelled along the lines of the Bhakra Beas Management Board (BBMB)
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: Frustrated that the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA) does not have the power to enforce its orders, Tamil Nadu is contemplating approaching the Supreme Court with a prayer that the Authority be given teeth.
It wants the Authority to be modelled along the lines of the Bhakra Beas Management Board (BBMB), a case of which has been mentioned in the Cauvery Water Disputes Tribunal’s report (Volume V).

Established in October 1967, the BBMB is engaged in the regulation of the supply of water and electricity from Bhakra Nangal and Beas projects to Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan, Himachal Pradesh, Delhi, and Chandigarh.

The CWMA chairperson Saumitra Kumar Haldar, too, in an interaction with The Hindu in August, referred to the Tribunal’s recommendation and explained that the Board, with the chief being appointed by the Union government, “owns, operates, manages, and regulates” the projects.
“They [the BBMB] take joint decisions regarding how much water is to be given and what the scheduling will be.
Everything is planned,” Mr. Haldar had said.

Tamil Nadu has been complaining that despite the quantities of water release stipulated by the CWMA in the last three-odd months being inadequate and lower than the proportionate share, the upper riparian State of Karnataka has not provided water, as per the mandated releases.

Of the seven spells of the 15-day water release ordered by the Authority since July 29, Karnataka has not complied with the release in five spells, even though, cumulatively, Tamil Nadu realised about 5,000 cubic feet per second (cusecs) higher than the total figure of 5.71 lakh cusecs, according to a persual of the data measured at Biligundulu on the inter-State border of Karnataka and Tamil Nadu.

As per the data available with the Central Water Commission, four reservoirs of Karnataka (Krishnaraja Sagara, Kabini, Hemavathi, and Harangi) registered a net cumulative inflow of about 132 thousand million cubic feet (tmc ft) during the period of June 1 to November 4, marking a shortfall of around 54%.
The 30-year-long average net inflow was around 288 tmc ft.

If the same shortfall is to be applied in the case of Tamil Nadu, the realisation should have been around 67 tmc ft between June 1 and November 4 against the quantum of approximately 145 tmc ft in a normal year.
But Biligundulu received 53.43 tmc ft only with a shortfall of around 13 tmc ft.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Monthly Roundup: September 2026
stories.title: Supreme Court Monthly Roundup: September 2026
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: Case Details: Anil Singh @ Anil Kumar Singh.
State of Bihar & Ors.

The Supreme Court cautioned the trial courts to proceed with alacrity during trial, especially when there is a total failure of the prosecution for not conducting examination of the crucial witnesses.
“…when there is total failure of the prosecution, the Court should with alacrity question the prosecution's conduct in not examining crucial witnesses.

The Trial Court is not a moot spectator and even in the role of an unbiased adjudicator has the responsibility to ensure that the best evidence is not suppressed by the prosecution…”, observed a bench of Justice J.B. Pardiwala and Justice K. Vinod Chandran, while setting aside the concurrent findings of the Patna High Court and Trial Court's order rejecting the de-facto complainant Section 311 Cr.P.C. application seeking examination of the crucial witness which could have a direct impact on the outcome of the trial.
The case arose from an altercation in which the appellant and his father sustained injuries.
Case Details: Ummed Devi.
State of Rajasthan and Anr.
The Supreme Court has disapproved of dismissing appeals on technical grounds like the absence of a delay condonation application when the litigant was not having proper legal assistance.
It is the duty of the Courts to ensure quality legal assistance to the litigants.

“True that the appeal should have been accompanied with an application for condonation of delay, but the Constitutional Courts should also be alive to the travails of a litigant and if the legal assistance is not adequate, it has a duty to provide quality legal assistance to the litigants, whether it be a victim or an accused.”, observed a bench of Justice J.B. Pardiwala and Justice K. Vinod Chandran, while setting aside the Rajasthan High Court's decision which had dismissed the appeal against an acquittal in a dowry death case merely for want of an application seeking condonation of delay with an appeal.
The victim's mother filed the appeal against the accused's acquittal before the High Court with a 19-day delay.

stories.headline: Cabinet nod to development of Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum at North and South Block complex
stories.title: Cabinet nod to development of Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum at North and South Block complex
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 11: The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs, in a meeting chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Wednesday, approved the development of the Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum through adaptive reuse of the North and South Block complex in Delhi, at an estimated total project cost of Rs 3,230 crore. It is envisaged as a landmark museum showcasing the continuity, diversity and richness of India's rich civilisational heritage through an integrated narrative of its tangible and intangible cultural heritage, according to officials. The museum will be developed through the adaptive reuse of the historic North and South Block complex, "preserving their architectural character and heritage significance while transforming them into a public cultural institution", the government said. Spread over a proposed built-up area of approximately 1,78,509 sq metres, the museum will integrate contemporary museum practices, immersive technologies and visitor-centric interpretation. Benchmarked against major international museums, the Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum is billed to be the museum with the largest display area in the world. "The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs, chaired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, today has approved the development of the Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum (YYBM) at the North and South Block Complex, New Delhi, at an estimated total project cost of Rs 3,230 crore, as appraised by the Public Investment Board (PIB)," the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) said. The ambitious museum project was announced by the prime minister on May 18, 2023.
